minutes.headline: Select Board moved a charter investigation into FY23 lakefront assessment spikes; the vote result is not in the captions.
minutes.summary: After a short liquor license hearing, the meeting was a large public question session with the principal assessor and two assessors about fiscal year 2023 land valuations on lakefront properties. The chair explained the abatement process and the February 1 payment deadline, and then moved an investigation under the town charter. Many residents spoke in public comment.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked to give a three-minute statistical presentation and was told to wait for public comment.
Asked why this has not happened in other towns with waterfront property.
Asked whether mismanagement of assessing since it came in-house caused a catch-up year; urged an investigation.
Argued the formula may violate Proposition 2.5 and suggested the attorney general.
Daughter read a statement for her ill veteran father about the burden of the tax increase on fixed income.
A realtor presented ten-year lake sales statistics and argued land values were inflated.
Urged a resolution stating no confidence in the assessment outcome.
Statement read for a senior on fixed income, proposing a cap on senior tax increases.
Asked for assurance that abatement applicants will be approved.
Asked why a size adjustment changed on their property.
Resident proposed paying the three-year average and skipping abatements; raised class action and media possibilities.
Former select board member said outsourced assessing from 1994 to 2020 had no such problem and asked to revisit that approach.
Homeowner described a 2020 purchase price versus the new assessment and asked for even assessments.
Announced an abatement help open house at Andrews Hall on Saturday.

votes.motion: Approve the all-alcohol restaurant license, common victualler license and weekday/Sunday entertainment license for La Bella Restaurante.

Under section 3-2e of the Town Charter, the select board conducts an investigation of COVID effects on 2021 property values, FY23 assessments and the valuation process; chair leads with vice chair and town manager.

budget_items.what_was_said: Town meeting allocated a set overlay amount, but assessors can abate beyond it; a larger cumulative figure is the point where abatements affect the budget.
A member said abatements reduce town revenue and could total millions out of the budget.
The chair explained the budget can grow only by the statutory percentage plus new growth absent a vote.

decisions.decision: Town manager to post RFPs for outside property assessors and work with staffing agencies for administrative support to the assessor's office.
Town to publish an answer on its website on whether abatement information can be added after February 1.
Next step is a roadmap and timeline for the investigation with routine public updates.

what_happened.line: The Select Board moved to open a Town Charter investigation into the effects of COVID on 2021 property values, fiscal 2023 assessments and the valuation process; the vote result is not audible.
The principal assessor and two assessors took resident questions on fiscal 2023 land valuations on lakefront properties for most of the meeting.
The chair explained the abatement process and the February 1 payment deadline, and how the levy limit and overlay bear on abatements.
The town manager is to post requests for proposals for outside assessors and seek staffing-agency help for the assessor's office.
Many residents spoke in public comment, including calls for an investigation, a cap on senior tax increases and a revisit of outsourced assessing.

why_it_matters: Lakefront owners facing higher fiscal 2023 assessments have an abatement route with a February 1 deadline, and the town has not yet said whether information can be added after that date.
Abatements granted beyond the overlay reduce town revenue, which can push the cost onto the budget and the tax rate for all taxpayers.
watch_next: The roadmap and timeline for the charter investigation, with routine public updates.
The town's published answer on whether abatement information can be added after February 1.
